papers.title: [Selenium-containing polyurethane-modified titanium modulates osteogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells and M2 polarization of macrophages].
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To address the issue of implant failure in clinical titanium implants due to inflammation, disease microenvironments, poor osseointegration through surface modification, and to explore the regulatory effects of selenium-containing biomaterial-modified titanium on the osteogenic differentiation of rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (rBMMSCs) and the M2 polarization of RAW 264.7 cells. METHODS: Selenium-containing polyurethane (SePU) was synthesized, and titanium sheets were modified by immersion in SePU solutions at concentrations of 1, 3, and 5 g/L. Pure titanium sheets served as the control group. rBMMSCs and RAW 264.7 cells were then cultured on the modified titanium surfaces. The surface contact angles of the SePU-modified titanium sheets were characterized. After 2 days of culture, the effect of SePU-modified titanium on the viability of rBMMSCs and RAW 264.7 cells was observed using live/dead cell staining. The osteogenic differentiation of rBMMSCs was evaluated using alkaline phosphatase (ALP) staining and quantification, alizarin red S (ARS) staining and quantification, as well as the expression levels of osteogenic-related genes. The polarization state of RAW 264.7 cells was assessed by analyzing the expression levels of macrophage polarization-related genes. RESULTS: SePU-modified titanium sheets were successfully prepared and their surface contact angles increased with the immersion concentration. Following 2 days of culture, the majority of rBMMSCs and RAW 264.7 cells on both the pure titanium and SePU-modified titanium surfaces were viable, with only a negligible presence of dead cells. Notably, compared with the pure titanium group, the SePU-modified titanium groups exhibited more profound ALP and ARS staining, coupled with a statistically significant increase in the expression levels of osteogenic-related genes (P < 0.05). Among these groups, the 3 g/L group showed the deepest ALP staining and the most significant increase in osteogenic-related gene expression. Furthermore, the SePU-modified titanium groups displayed decreased expression of proinflammatory genes and increased expression of anti-inflammatory genes compared with the unmodified pure titanium group, with statistically significant differences (P < 0.05). The 3 g/L group exhibited the most significant effect among the modified titanium groups. CONCLUSION: SePU-modified titanium not only exhibits increased surface contact angles but also has no significant effect on cell viability. It effectively promotes the osteogenic differentiation of rBMMSCs and the M2 polarization of RAW 264.7 cells, indicating its potential for enhancing bone regeneration and modulating immune responses in biomedical applications.

papers.title: Preoperative whey protein and exercise ımprove early recovery after total hip arthroplasty: a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is an effective surgical procedure for treating hip osteoarthritis; however, postoperative recovery may be complicated by impaired functional capacity, delayed mobilization, and prolonged hospital stay. Preoperative multimodal strategies combining nutritional support and exercise may improve recovery outcomes. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the effects of a combined multimodal prehabilitation protocol (preoperative whey protein supplementation plus structured exercise) on metabolic parameters, functional independence, and length of hospital stay in patients undergoing THA. Methods This randomized controlled trial included 71 patients scheduled for total hip arthroplasty (THA). Participants were randomly assigned to either the intervention group (n = 36), which received a 14-day preoperative program consisting of oral whey protein supplementation (25 g/day) and a partially supervised, home-based structured exercise protocol (comprising an initial face-to-face instruction followed by telephone-guided monitoring), or the control group (n = 35), which received standard care. Baseline habitual physical activity levels were recorded for both groups. Data were collected preoperatively and on postoperative days 3 and 5. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Barthel Index, while biochemical markers included C-reactive protein (CRP) and albumin levels. Statistical analyses included ANCOVA (adjusting for age and chronic diseases) and Repeated-Measures ANOVA for longitudinal markers. Results Significant Group × Time interaction effects were observed for CRP ( p < 0.001) and albumin ( p = 0.008), indicating different postoperative trajectories between the intervention and control groups. After adjustment for age and chronic disease status, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher Barthel Index scores than the control group ( p < 0.001; ηp 2 = 0.31), with a large standardized between-group effect (Cohen’s d = 1.59). Length of hospital stay was significantly shorter in the intervention group (5.11 ± 1.38 vs. 6.94 ± 1.72 days); this difference remained statistically significant after adjustment for age and chronic disease status ( p = 0.004). Conclusion Combined preoperative multimodal prehabilitation integrating whey protein supplementation with structured exercise demonstrates promising efficacy in improving early functional recovery and reducing length of hospital stay in patients undergoing THA. While baseline imbalances necessitate a cautious interpretation of the effect magnitude, this integrated strategy shows strong clinical potential for perioperative optimization. Trial registration : The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07329010) on 25 September 2025.

papers.title: ADAPTIVE LIGHTWEIGHT STRUCTURAL DESIGN FRAMEWORK FOR ALUMINIUM TRAILER PLATFORMS USING MULTI-OBJECTIVE FINITE ELEMENT OPTIMIZATION AND MANUFACTURABILITY CONSTRAINTS
papers.abstract: Adaptive lightweight design of aluminum trailer platforms is technically significant, as road-load requirements, payload, stiffness, fatigue, buckling, and manufacturability requirements often conflict. The review critically summarizes the published journal literature concerning multi-objective finite element optimization, manufacturing-oriented topology optimization, joining of aluminum, stress/buckling control and lightweight vehicle-related structural design. The literature review demonstrates that effective lightweight designs were not necessarily achieved by minimizing weight, but rather by considering the following factors: load-path continuity, minimum member size, weld access, structural feasibility of the trailer platform, interaction between the deck and the trailer platform, fatigue-prone details and the avoidance of local buckling. Existing research is well-grounded in the computational aspects, but is scattered over vehicle crashworthiness, aerospace topology optimization, additive manufacturing limitations, and general aluminum fabrication research. Validation of trailers, multi-objective optimization considering fatigue and the rules of manufacture of welded and extruded aluminum remain insufficiently developed. Such a framework should therefore integrate finite element fidelity, surrogate model adaptation, manufacturable geometry production, and production-based constraint screening.

papers.title: UNCERTAINTY QUANTIFICATION AND CARRIER-COLLECTION ROBUSTNESS UNDER PHYSICAL TOLERANCES IN A SERIES VERTICAL-JUNCTION SILICON SOLAR CELL
papers.abstract: This work investigates the propagation of uncertainties in physical parameters to carrier collection in a series vertical-junction silicon solar cell. Starting from an exact dimensionless collection law, uncertainties are introduced in the base thickness H, diffusion coefficient D, carrier lifetime τ, and interface recombination velocities Sf and Sb. For each realization, the diffusion length and the reduced parameters h, f, and b are recalculated, thereby preserving the dependencies induced by the physical transformation. Twenty-seven nominal regimes and four controlled uncertainty amplitudes, from ±5% to ±30%, are investigated using a Monte Carlo campaign of 120,000 realizations per scenario. Robustness is characterized by the coefficient of variation of collection and by R90 = P(C ≥ 0.9 C0). The median coefficient of variation increases from approximately 3.13% at ±5% to 18.94% at ±30%, while the maximum value reaches 37.14%. Over the same range, the median R90 decreases from 100% to approximately 68.12%. At ±30%, some regimes retain R90 close to unity, whereas the least robust regime in the grid reaches approximately 60.17%. The regime of maximum statistical dispersion does not exactly coincide with that of minimum R90. These results show that nominal performance, statistical dispersion, and probabilistic robustness are distinct properties and establish a regime-dependent map for assessing collection robustness under controlled physical uncertainty.

papers.title: Rapid Recovery in Patients After Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) While Using Digital Health
papers.abstract: Digital health is currently used for many health conditions with more being added frequently. One use case is recovery from a Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA). This study looked at patients who used Plethy’s Recupe digital health platform to supplement medical and physical therapy care after their THA. The Recupe mobile app guided patients through prescribed recovery exercises and activities. The Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS), which has been well validated through research, was used as an objective measure for this recovery. With an average age of 65 for males and 68 for females and BMI of around 30, the population was similar to the averages seen in other studies. Patients used the digital health app an average of 134 days for females and 119 days for males, indicating frequent use of digital health to assist with their exercises and activities. From this, HOOS scores improved 19 points for females and 24 points for males, more than the minimal clinically important difference. Pain also decreased 2.7/10 for men and 3.0/10 for women. From these results, digital health appears to show promise as part of a recovery protocol after THA. It is important to note that digital health is a supplementary adjunct, not a replacement for care.

papers.title: Fatigue Crack Growth and Stress‐Based Assessment of a Wind Turbine Main‐Bearing Model Under Simulated and Monitoring‐Based Inputs
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Wind turbine main‐bearing crack assessment requires consistent treatment of material crack growth and operating‐load uncertainty. Fatigue crack‐growth tests were performed on GCr15 0.5‐T CT specimens at , 0.10, and 0.50, and Paris parameters were identified. Finite element simulation at agreed with experiments within 15%. A laboratory‐scale NU205E surrogate was then used for static contact analyses with prescribed semielliptical raceway cracks. Increasing surface‐crack length caused a nonlinear rise in maximum von Mises stress, whereas increasing crack depth reduced the local maximum because of stress redistribution. A normalized Basquin‐based fatigue‐life index was used only for comparative assessment. The monitoring response–based equivalent input produced higher local stresses than the simulated input, increasing inner‐ and outer‐raceway peaks by 16.7% and 26.4%, respectively. The framework distinguishes local stress response from fracture mechanics–based remaining life.

papers.title: Bioactive and Nanomodified Titanium Surfaces for Preventing Early Osseointegration Failure: Can Smart Biomaterials Simultaneously Enhance Osteogenesis and Resist Bacterial Colonization? A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Early failure of titanium dental implants remains a significant clinical challenge, arising from a multifactorial interplay of poor primary stability, impaired osteoblastic differentiation, early bacterial contamination of the implant interface, host systemic factors and excessive micromotion during the initial healing period. Because implant surface topography and chemistry directly govern early protein adsorption and the subsequent osteogenic cell signalling cascade, the design of the titanium surface has become a central focus of strategies aimed at reducing early failure rates. The objective of this narrative review was to evaluate whether bioactive and nanomodified titanium surface coatings can simultaneously enhance osteogenesis and inhibit bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation and to examine the biological, antimicrobial and clinical evidence supporting these multifunctional surface modifications. Literature was retrieved from PubMed, Google Scholar and ScienceDirect, covering studies published between 2021 and 2026 and included clinical studies, in-vitro and in-vivo investigations and original research. Antibacterial surface modifications reduced bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation while generally maintaining biocompatibility and supporting osseointegration. Silver, zinc, copper and titanium dioxide nanomaterials, antimicrobial peptides, nitric oxide releasing systems and other coatings demonstrated promising broad spectrum antibacterial effects, although further standardized studies are needed. Bioactive and nanomodified titanium surfaces appear to improve the early bone response and may also help limit bacterial adhesion and biofilm development. The current evidence is nevertheless insufficient to confirm a clear long term clinical advantage over conventional implant surfaces and more standardized clinical studies with longer follow up are required.

papers.title: Parkinson’s disease is associated with increased 90-day readmission and reoperation after elective total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD) undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) may be at increased risk for postoperative complications due to neuromuscular dysfunction and medical frailty. Contemporary national data on short-term outcomes following elective primary THA in this population remain limited. This study evaluated index hospitalization complications and 90-day readmission with procedural escalation after elective primary THA in patients with PD. We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Nationwide Readmissions Database (2020–2022). Adult patients undergoing elective primary THA on hospital day 0 were identified. A variable-ratio propensity score-matched cohort of up to 1:5 (PD: non-PD) was constructed using demographics, payer, hospital characteristics, calendar year, and comorbidities (all standardized mean differences < 0.1). Index complications, 90-day readmission, and readmission-associated procedural escalation (any procedure, reoperation, and revision) were assessed. The matched cohort included 12,143 elective primary THAs (2,043 PD; 10,100 controls). PD was associated with higher rates of perioperative complications, including blood transfusion, pneumonia, urinary tract infection, and hip dislocation (all p ≤ 0.015), while in-hospital mortality remained low and similar between groups. Within 90 days, PD patients had higher readmission (10.3% vs. 5.8%; OR 1.86; p < 0.001) and markedly increased procedural escalation, including reoperation (3.3% vs. 0.9%) and revision (3.0% vs. 0.7%) (all p < 0.001). Length of stay was longer in PD patients, with no significant difference in hospital charges. Elective primary THA in patients with Parkinson’s disease is associated with increased perioperative complications and substantially higher 90-day readmission with early revision and reoperation. These findings highlight increased post-discharge vulnerability in this population and underscore the need for enhanced perioperative optimization and postoperative surveillance.

papers.title: CONTEXT-AWARE DIGITAL TWIN ARCHITECTURES FOR REAL-TIME TRANSPORTATION AND WAREHOUSE OPTIMIZATION IN CLOUD-NATIVE SUPPLY CHAIN PLATFORMS
papers.abstract: Context-aware digital twins are emerging as enabling architectures for coordinating responses to disruptions across inventory, warehouse, and transportation operations in cloud-based supply-chain platforms. They are important because they can be used to link continually evolving operational representations with optimization services that are able to react to traffic conditions, order arrivals, equipment status, changes in inventory, and facility constraints. This article reviews peer-reviewed journal literature on digital supply-chain twins, warehouse intelligence, dynamic vehicle routing, Internet of Things-enabled logistics, microservice architectures, and computational modelling. Some studies indicate that digital-twin approaches can improve visibility, scenario evaluation, and decision coordination in specific settings, but there is very little evidence of fully integrated real-time optimization of transportation and warehouse operations. Closed-loop orchestration has not been a primary focus of existing implementations, which tend to focus on warehouse simulation or monitoring, route adjustment, or resilience analysis across logistics domains. Other limitations include insufficient semantic interoperability, inadequate model fidelity, inconsistent latency assessment, deployment evidence, and consideration of cybersecurity and human intervention. The field therefore needs architectures that integrates event-driven context management, federated twin models, scalable optimization, auditable decision services, and explicit uncertainty handling.

papers.title: Integrated Vibration Energy Harvesting and Structural Vibration Control: A State-of-the-Art Review of Electro-Mechanical Co-Design
papers.abstract: Vibration energy harvesters and vibration control devices have been typically designed as two distinct subsystems, one to harvest a small electrical output, and the other to reduce a mechanical response. The efficiency of the separation is becoming less and less efficient as the same electromechanical coupling which converts the strain or relative motion to electricity also alters the effective damping, stiffness, impedance and frequency response of the host structure. This paper summarizes the current status of integrated vibration energy harvesting and structural vibration control and focuses on co-design of the electro-mechanical systems. The field is organized for the review: transduction mechanism, integration architecture, control authority and bandwidth strategy. A unified energy-flow and coupled-dynamics framework is used to compare the performance of piezoelectric shunts, electromagnetic shunt dampers, energy-regenerative tuned mass dampers, nonlinear energy sinks, hybrid piezoelectric-electromagnetic devices, and triboelectric metamaterials and distributed piezoelectric metastructures. The overall finding is that performance should be judged in terms of a Pareto problem with respect to vibration response, harvested power, bandwidth, mass, control energy, reliability and implementation complexity, not on a single peak-power or attenuation norm. Passive systems and semi-active systems are most close to being practically deployed because they are self powered or nearly self powered and have a greater level of adaptability, but they will need to be carefully powered. Further advancements will rely on source-spectrum characterization, circuit-aware structural optimization, uncertainty quantification, durability testing and field testing and validation. A co design workflow is suggested to be developed to integrate mathematical models, multi-objective optimization and deployable sensing/ isolation systems.

papers.title: High-Quality, Low-Cost Quasi-Bulk Hexagonal Boron Nitride Crystals by LP-HVPE: Machine Learning-Assisted Process Optimization via XRD and Raman Characterization
papers.abstract: Abstract Highly ordered, quasi-bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) films were grown on c-plane sapphire (α-Al2O3) substrates via low-pressure hydride vapor-phase epitaxy (LP-HVPE), using industrial-grade boron trichloride (BCl3) and ammonia (NH3) as low-cost boron and nitrogen sources, respectively. The effects of four key growth parameters (growth temperature, III/V source flow ratio, growth ambient, and growth pressure) on the crystalline quality of hBN films were systematically investigated via the single-variable method. A gradient boosting regression machine learning (ML) model was constructed based on 24 groups of experimental datasets to achieve high-precision prediction of hBN crystalline quality, with determination coefficients (R2) of 0.96 and 0.94 for the prediction of X-ray diffraction and Raman characteristic peak full width at half maximum, respectively. The optimized growth condition was determined as follows: a growth temperature of 1350 °C, a III/V ratio of 1:3, N2 ambient, and a growth pressure of 100 Pa, which is consistent with the global optimal parameters obtained by Bayesian optimization combined with the ML model. This work provides a low-cost, high-efficiency route for the controllable preparation of high-quality quasi-bulk hBN crystals via LP-HVPE with ML-assisted optimization.

papers.title: Robotics Capable of Development. Coordinate Seeds for Tolerance Fields, Relational Ontogeny, Physical Preconditioning and Learning World Organization
papers.abstract: This conceptual synthesis and discussion paper explores how robotic systems capable of long-term development might be conceived and designed when the central question is not maximum precision or the most complete possible world model, but which distinctions actually matter for a particular action and its consequences. Starting from everyday manipulation tasks, the paper develops conceptual tools such as tolerance fields, catchment regions and competence funnels. It examines how the design of bodies, mechanics, sensors and environments can physically prestructure complexity so that subsequent control and learning processes face a better-conditioned problem. This perspective is described in terms of physical preconditioning. The concepts of cut (Schnitt), cut literacy (Schnittkundigkeit) and coordinate seeds direct attention to how relevant distinctions and variables emerge, prove useful and remain revisable. An organization capable of development would not merely learn within predetermined categories but, under appropriate conditions, could also refine, combine or reopen its distinctions in response to the world. Further topics include adaptive perceptual resolution, learning from near-miss events, protected environments for exploration, the sedimentation of experience into presently effective competences, and relational and collective ontogeny. Everyday examples, connections to established research, proposed experiments and counter-hypotheses are used to open possible directions for technical and scientific investigation. The paper does not present a completed robotics architecture or a systematic literature review. Its proposed contribution is a conceptual synthesis of existing and further questions, a set of distinctions intended to prevent premature conflations, and potentially testable research directions. No claim of scientific priority over related work is made.

papers.title: Sacrificial‐Template Fabrication of Orientation‐Controlled Porous Titanium Lattices With Bioactive Surfaces
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Porous titanium scaffolds for bone repair require coordinated control of pore architecture, mechanical behavior, and surface bioactivity. Here, we report a sacrificial‐template route based on polymer 3D printing that produces orientation‐controlled porous titanium scaffolds with hierarchical macro‐ and microporosity without direct metal additive manufacturing. Polylactic acid lattices printed by fused deposition modeling are infiltrated with a titanium powder slurry and then subjected to template removal and sintering. The process yields ortho‐grid, tri‐lattice, and quad‐lattice structures with approximately 26% isotropic linear shrinkage, 65%–67% porosity, preserved geometric fidelity, and a relative density of approximately 95% in the sintered strut walls. Uniaxial compression tests reveal architecture‐dependent behavior along the tested loading direction, whereas finite element simulations predict lower directional sensitivity under off‐axis loading as strut‐orientation diversity increases. Micro‐arc oxidation forms a Ca–P‐containing microporous oxide layer and improves cell spreading, proliferation, and alkaline phosphatase activity relative to untreated titanium scaffolds in vitro. In a rat calvarial defect model, uncoated titanium scaffolds achieve bone regeneration comparable to commercial porous tantalum, while micro‐arc oxidation further enhances bone formation. Fabrication of cone augments and other non‐prismatic geometries further demonstrates the adaptability of the approach to complex implant‐relevant structures.

papers.title: Data Augmentation‐Driven Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Operational Amplifiers With Improved Conformal Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate remaining useful life prediction is critical to the reliable operation of operational amplifiers in modern electronic systems. However, existing methods face two key challenges: predictions typically lack statistical guarantees on uncertainty quantification (UQ), and randomly missing monitoring data caused by sensor or transmission failures further degrade model performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a data augmentation‐driven RUL prediction and conformal UQ method, termed DiffUQ. First, an Electronic Component Degradation Pattern Encoder (ECDPE) is constructed by integrating contrastive learning into a variational autoencoder framework to extract discriminative degradation representations from multivariate monitoring data. Building on these representations, a diffusion‐based data generation framework (DiffGen) equipped with a specially designed ST‐Denoiser is developed to impute and augment data with missing values while capturing the underlying spatio‐temporal correlations. Finally, deep metric learning is combined with enhanced conformal prediction to construct prediction intervals that retain a coverage guarantee under departures from exchangeability, with the loss of coverage bounded explicitly. Experiments on the accelerated degradation dataset of SX8042MF operational amplifiers demonstrate that DiffUQ achieves superior point prediction accuracy and uncertainty quantification compared to several state‐of‐the‐art baselines under various missing‐data ratios. Moreover, DiffGen consistently improves multiple underlying prediction models and outperforms widely used data augmentation methods such as CGAN, WGAN‐GP, VAE, and TimeVAE.

papers.title: A Reduced-Order Model for the High-Field Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System Based on a Micro-Macro Decomposition
papers.abstract: We develop a projection-based reduced-order model for the high-field Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system. Based on a micro-macro decomposition, the proposed Micro-ROM applies proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)-Galerkin reduction only to the microscopic fluctuation while retaining the macroscopic density on the full spatial grid. The field-dependent Maxwellian and collision operator introduce additional computational costs that cannot be eliminated by Galerkin projection alone. To remove the dependence on the velocity-grid resolution during online simulations, we approximate the projected Maxwellian terms using precomputed Chebyshev expansions of functions of the local electric field and exploit a separable discretization of the collision operator to assemble the reduced collision matrix exactly from precomputed blocks. A first-order implicit-explicit scheme is employed to evolve the reduced coefficients and the density. The resulting method conserves discrete mass and formally recovers a discretization of the limiting high-field model as $\varepsilon\rightarrow 0$. Its online computational cost per time step is independent of the velocity-grid resolution. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method across a range of parameters, including the high-field regime.

papers.title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
papers.abstract: Bone scaffolds must reconcile a macroscale mechanical response with microscale geometric feasibility, yet conventional approaches to their design restrict attainable constitutive properties. This work presents a concurrent two-scale topology optimization framework; a conditional rectified flow generates periodic lattice microstructures, which are then refined in latent space by exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities. The resulting unit-cell geometries and their spatial assignments are jointly optimized under mechanical and feature-size constraints. In a distal rabbit femur benchmark, all eight flow-started refinements produce printable cells with maximum relative errors under 1\% across six prescribed engineering moduli. Constructing the implant from a single tiled cell reproduces intact whole-femur compliance within 0.1\% and regional strain energy within 0.35\% under four loading conditions. In human femoral reconstruction, multiscale concurrent optimization produces a cortical mid-shaft scaffold with porosity 63\% while satisfying the compliance constraint within 2\% under walking and stair-climbing loads. It achieves an 84\% porosity on a proximal cancellous scaffold with strain-energy deviations below 0.25\% under the same loads. Analysis of the learned representations reveals distinct architectural families in latent space. Further, the attention heads of the rectified-flow transformer specialize for spatial shifts -- learning the analogue of a finite-difference stencil -- and coordinate symmetries, with ablations showing their influence on generated topologies. These results establish a route to printable, mechanically constrained scaffold designs. The framework is general enough for extending to many other multiscale structural design applications including topology-microstructure co-design in metal additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Self-Supervised In-Context Operator Learning for Optimal Mixing in Incompressible Flows
papers.abstract: We develop a self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing in incompressible flows, aimed at overcoming the computational limitations of classical PDE-constrained optimal control. The objective is to design velocity fields that efficiently homogenize a passive scalar while minimizing kinetic energy, quantified through the $\dot H^{-1}(Ω)$ mix-norm. Classical methods solve a separate optimal control problem for each initial condition using iterative forward-adjoint procedures, leading to substantial computational costs and limited scalability. In contrast, we propose to learn the solution operator that maps initial scalar fields to optimal mixing controls directly. The proposed self-supervised method does not require access to supervised labels, thereby significantly reducing the data-generation burden of supervised operator-learning methods. Our framework integrates a Lagrangian reformulation of the transport equation with a transformer-based neural operator architecture. The transport dynamics are represented through characteristic ODEs, enabling particle-based Monte Carlo optimization, while the learned velocity field is parameterized in a divergence-free spectral basis enforcing incompressibility and no-penetration conditions exactly. Numerical experiments on parametric families of initial conditions in two and three spatial dimensions demonstrate robust generalization to unseen regimes and approximately exponential decay of the mix-norm. The learned controls also transfer consistently to independent Eulerian finite-volume simulations, validating the physical fidelity of the learned operator. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing and among the first data-driven approaches for optimal mixing in fully three-dimensional incompressible flows.

papers.title: Dynamics-Aligned Representation Learning under Induced Partial Observability
papers.abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) has enabled sample-efficient learning of continuous control policies from high-dimensional observations through learned latent dynamics models. These models are typically trained with observation reconstruction objectives, which provide strong supervision but can bias representations toward visual fidelity leading to an undertrained prior and unreliable long-horizon predictions. We propose a stochastic gating mechanism that induces controlled partial observability during training by sampling a spatial binary mask from a Beta--Bernoulli random field and applying it to the raw observation. The gate probability is resampled at each time step, exposing the encoder to conditions ranging from near-total occlusion to near-full visibility. Integration of our method requires minimal architectural changes from existing dynamics models: the gated observation and the binary mask are channel-wise concatenated and passed to the encoder as a single augmented input, with no modifications to the broader training pipeline. We evaluate the proposed approach on a set of pixel-based continuous control tasks selected from the DeepMind Control Suite. Using model predictive control for evaluation, which relies solely on open-loop model rollouts, we show that stochastic gating improves planning performance and data efficiency across tasks. Further analysis demonstrates that performance is robust to the spatial scale of the mask, and a balanced observability during training outperforms configurations biased toward either sparser or denser observations.

papers.title: CusADi2: Latency-Optimized Batch Computation of Robot Kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians on the GPU
papers.abstract: Trajectory optimization methods, from sampling-based zero-order to gradient-based first- and second-order approaches, require many evaluations of dynamical system functions, i.e., functions derived from a robot's dynamical model, such as forward kinematics and their Jacobians and Hessians. These evaluations are largely independent, e.g., across sampled trajectories or time steps, and can thus be evaluated in parallel as a batch. When used to make decisions online, these methods require low latency, i.e., each batch must complete in as little wall-clock time as possible. Existing frameworks utilize modern GPU hardware primarily to parallelize across batch instances, thereby optimizing throughput but not latency. We present CusADi2, a software library that reduces the batch evaluation latency by additionally parallelizing computation within each batch instance. We benchmark forward kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians for all 67~robots in the MuJoCo Menagerie, including arms, hands, quadrupeds, humanoids, and biomechanical models, against MuJoCo XLA, MuJoCo Warp, frax, CusADi, and CasADi. CusADi2 achieves lower latency than all baselines at batch sizes of 64 to 4096, while matching them at larger batch sizes. We also demonstrate the performance advantage of CusADi2 in a sampling-based control application. All code is open-source at: https://github.com/johnviljoen/cusadi2

papers.title: Intent-Informed Model Predictive Control for Shared Autonomy in Remote Manipulation Tasks
papers.abstract: Shared autonomy is a control paradigm that combines human cognitive abilities with robot precision to enable effective remote manipulation in complex environments. A key challenge is how to adapt the level of autonomy using information extracted from the human, task, and/or environment. In this paper, we propose a novel arbitration strategy that dynamically adjusts the level of autonomy in the system using the entropy of a belief distribution derived from a multimodal intent inference. Human intent is modeled with a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN), which updates beliefs over goals given real-time operator gaze data and robot arm motion during teleoperation. We then formulate the blending of human input and autonomous control as a Model Predictive Control (MPC) problem, where the system's autonomous behavior is guided by the belief distribution. This approach enables continuous, gradual transitions across the full spectrum of autonomy levels, from direct teleoperation to full autonomy. To validate our approach, we conducted experiments to compare the performance of our proposed algorithm against two MPC-based shared autonomy methods. Compared to the baselines, our approach achieved reductions of at least 61% in object retrieval time, 44% in trajectory length, and 60% in human control input. Participants reported high perceived control, predictability, intent recognition, and responsiveness, along with low workload.

papers.title: DR-Learners for Generalizing CATEs from a Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.abstract: Randomized clinical trials are essential for evaluating interventions, yet average treatment effects can obscure treatment effect heterogeneity, making conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) a natural target. However, restrictive eligibility criteria and differential trial participation can limit the generalizability of these effects to broader target populations. Building on existing DR-Learners, we develop the gDR-Learner for generalizing RCT CATEs to a target population, using cross-fitted machine-learning nuisance estimation. We derive excess-risk bounds in which nuisance errors enter only as products, showing that the estimator achieves oracle-rate convergence despite slower individual nuisance estimation. The variables needed to generalize are rarely measured across the entire target population. We therefore extend the methods to two settings with incomplete covariate information: when certain covariates are measured only in the trial (e.g., biomarkers), and covariates driving trial participation measured only in a subsample of the target population, such as a representative cohort or registry. We construct weighted conformal prediction intervals for individual treatment effects, accounting for covariate shift between the trial and target population. In simulations, the gDR-Learner achieved the lowest estimation error when all covariates were observed relative to standard T- and DR-Learners and an inverse-probability-weighted T-Learner, and also outperformed the latter under incomplete covariate observation. We illustrate the methods by reanalyzing the Coronary Artery Surgery Study, examining treatment effect heterogeneity by prior myocardial infarction and baseline ejection fraction.

papers.title: Predicted Class Correction: Conformal Thresholds for Classes with No Calibration Data
papers.abstract: Class-conditional conformal prediction calibrates a separate score threshold for every class and therefore requires labelled calibration examples of every class. In long-tailed deployments these are exactly what is missing: rare classes are left with few or no held-out examples, and existing methods are either undefined for them or fall back to the shared marginal threshold. We ask whether the per-class correction can instead be predicted from descriptors of the class that require no labels at all. We propose Predicted Class Correction (PCC), which regresses the offset between the per-class and the marginal conformal quantile on geometric descriptors of the classifier head, shrinks the prediction by a scalar selected on the labelled classes, and refits a single marginal offset. The descriptors depend only on the model's weights, so a class with zero calibration examples still receives its own threshold, and since only one scalar is calibrated, split conformal's marginal guarantee is retained. On ImageNet, PCC improves worst-class coverage on such classes by 0.058 [0.006, 0.110] at matched average set size, 42% of an oracle that sees the test labels. Of eight baselines on the same splits, six change the statistic by exactly zero and the best reaches 0.016 with an interval containing zero, so PCC is the only one distinguishable from no improvement; the gain persists with only 100 labelled classes out of 1000. A second finding concerns evaluation: worst-class coverage becomes unmeasurable before it becomes unachievable. Below roughly 35 test examples per class no improvement can be shown even for an oracle, so a null result there reflects the evaluation set, not the method. Restricting evaluation above this depth recovers a significant improvement on Pl@ntNet-300K, where the effect had appeared absent.

papers.title: World Model Interpretability: From Decoding Representations to Understanding Latent Worlds
papers.abstract: Emerging Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are moving beyond representation learning towards latent world models that support prediction, planning, and control. Yet their latent worlds naturally lack a human-interpretable interface. In this Perspective, we argue that as JEPA latents become internal states for prediction and action, interpretability must move beyond what they encode to how latent variables interact, evolve, and causally drive prediction. To this end, we envision a four-stage research agenda, involving Ground, Structure, Verify, and Act, to guide this shift toward actionable latent-world understanding. Within our framework, existing JEPA interpretability efforts provide early evidence for Ground, while systematic analysis of latent structure, causal verification, and intervention remains largely unexplored. Overall, this Perspective aims to call for a broader latent-world interpretability agenda that shifts attention from decoding representations toward understanding, validating, and acting on latent worlds.

papers.title: Data-driven forecasting of tropical cloud forest phenology: A dynamical systems and machine learning hybrid approach
papers.abstract: Forecasting how species and ecosystems respond to climate change is a critical challenge in ecology, particularly in hyper-diverse tropical biomes. While traditional phenological models often rely on preconceived functional forms, this study introduces a data-driven hybrid approach that integrates dynamical systems theory with machine learning to forecast flowering and fruiting cycles.   Using a robust 35-year dataset from a Venezuelan tropical cloud forest, we reconstruct the system's state-space using delay vectors inspired by Takens' theorem, incorporating climate forcing variables such as temperature and precipitation. The model was trained using Gaussian Process Regression, providing both point predictors and explicit uncertainty estimates.   Our results clearly suggest that the synergy between dynamical systems and machine learning effectively captures the non-linear complexities of ecological time series. Specifically, the model achieved higher predictive accuracy for flowering and fruiting. This hybrid framework offers a scalable tool for anticipating phenological mismatches and informing conservation strategies in the face of global environmental change.

papers.title: World Models, Trees and Foundation Models for Retail Forecasting: Evidence from Four Public Data Sets
papers.abstract: A retailer makes different decisions at different grains of the product, store and time hierarchy: store orders for an item in a store, supplier funding for an item across stores, category performance by store, and the financial plan for the chain. Which forecasting model to use depends on the grain. This paper compares models at each grain on four public data sets (M5, six Dominick's categories, Breakfast at the Frat, and Corporación Favorita, the last kept out of all development), over rolling forecast origins with paired tests and model confidence sets. It covers price and promotion through the plan inputs these data record, not product, assortment or place. The models are a world model that carries each item's state forward under the price and promotion plan, the same network without that state, LightGBM, the Temporal Fusion Transformer, TimesFM, Chronos-Bolt, Timestral, seasonal naive, and an equal-weight average of the world model, LightGBM and TimesFM given the plan. The answer changed with the grain. For an item by store and an item across stores, the average had the lowest error on seven and eight of nine data sets, and the 90% confidence set held a median of 1 and 2 models. For a category by store, a category and the chain total, the lowest-error model differed between data sets and a median of 4 of nine models were not separated by the four to six windows available. For category-by-store planning cost, the average or LightGBM was lowest on seven of eight data sets, and the world model was lowest only on M5; it was behind LightGBM item by store on six of eight. Every trained model used the plan, and on the weekly promotion-driven data pretrained models were less accurate without it. These results hold for these data sets; a forecast solved across all four Ps, or a retailer's own data, may give different results. Every model, test and change that lost is reported.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization for Reasoning Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning improves the reasoning capability of large language models through verifiable rewards for mathematical and coding tasks. In token-level methods such as GRPO, clipping acts on individual token ratios while the reward and advantage apply to a complete response. Recent sequence-level methods align these units but still use fixed clipping bands, whose tail probabilities change as the score distribution evolves. We propose Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization (CSPO), which adaptively calibrates sequence-level clipping bounds using recent training statistics. The resulting band targets a specified marginal tail budget and adapts to policy drift; calibration conditional on response length requires additional assumptions. We bound the probability that a fresh score falls outside the band by the target miscoverage level plus explicit CDF discrepancy and drift terms. papers.abstract: Multifidelity Monte Carlo (MFMC) reduces the cost of estimating the statistics of quantities of interest (QoIs) computed via expensive high-fidelity model by using cheaper low-fidelity models as control variates. We extend MFMC to vector-valued QoIs by replacing the scalar control-variate coefficients with matrices and minimizing a weighted mean-squared error. The optimal full-matrix coefficients are available in closed form, and their variance reduction is summarized by an effective correlation that takes the place of the squared Pearson correlation in the closed-form MFMC design. Restricting the coefficients to block-diagonal, diagonal, and scalar classes gives a nested hierarchy of estimators with increasing variance reduction and increasing pilot-data demand, with closed-form coefficients for compatible weightings. For a scalar QoI obtained by linearly projecting the state, correcting the full state before projecting is never worse at the population level. Experiments on a Gaussian problem, a reduced-order model of an advection--diffusion problem, and a coarse-grid two-phase flow problem show that the best class depends on the pilot size relative to the number of covariance quantities it must estimate, and that reusing the pilot samples lowers the mean-squared error.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT This study experimentally and numerically investigates fatigue damage in additively manufactured 316L stainless steel produced by selective laser melting using the powder bed fusion–laser beam process. More than 100 specimens were tested under tensile and strain‐controlled fatigue loading to evaluate the effects of surface condition, hot isostatic pressing (HIP), and build orientation. Machining provides the greatest improvement in fatigue performance by removing sub‐surface defects, while HIP provides additional benefits through reduced porosity. Vertically built specimens exhibit approximately 40% longer fatigue life than diagonal and horizontal specimens because elongated grains aligned with the build direction enhance ductility and stabilize crack propagation. A unified continuum damage mechanics‐based constitutive model predicts cyclic softening and fatigue life across low‐ and high‐cycle regimes. Fatigue anisotropy is represented by an orientation‐dependent fatigue ductility coefficient, while remaining parameters are orientation‐independent. The model accurately reproduces cyclic hysteresis loops and fatigue life to failure.

Accurate modal identification is essential for understanding instability mechanisms and optimizing combustor design and control. To address the modeling and identification of unstable thermoacoustic dynamics, this study proposes a physics-informed data-driven framework with a corresponding training strategy and verifies its feasibility using numerical simulations of a Rijke tube, a classical simplified thermoacoustic combustor model. By embedding the governing equations of the thermoacoustic combustor system within the PINN framework, the proposed data-driven PINN can accurately identify and separate the first and second acoustic modes under conditions of strong thermoacoustic coupling. Furthermore, under a well-designed training strategy, the framework can simultaneously accomplish mode identification and parameter discovery even when certain system parameters are unknown. Multiple training trials indicate that the method exhibits satisfactory robustness to external noise, suggesting potential for engineering applications in thermoacoustic combustor modeling and monitoring.

papers.title: Dynamics-aware scheduling of renewable electrolyzer plants: A physics-informed reinforcement learning approach
papers.abstract: Producing hydrogen via renewable electrolyzer plants (REPs) is crucial for reducing carbon emissions in industrial sectors. Meanwhile, with renewable energy generation and electrolyzer units integrated at a common grid connection, these plants provide high-quality resources for regulating power grid operations. Nonetheless, fully utilizing this potential relies on the profitable operation of REPs across joint energy and frequency containment reserve markets in conjunction with the application of data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) scheduling approaches to counteract the stochasticity in renewable generation and the volatility of markets. However, current scheduling frameworks often neglect detailed internal thermal-electrical dynamics and discrete operational states, which result in sub-optimal or physically infeasible policies. The present work addresses this issue by proposing a comprehensive imitation-enhanced RL (IE-RL) scheduling framework. First, the framework incorporates a physics-informed neural network surrogate model to capture transient electrolyzer dynamics accurately. Then, the operational environment is decoupled into continuous subspaces based on whether the electrolyzer unit is in the on state or in the standby state, and dedicated expert policies are pre-trained for each operational environment. Finally, the IE-RL agent is trained to imitate the expert policy matching the current active operational state accurately. The results of numerical computations demonstrate that the proposed approach enhances joint-market profitability while maintaining high physical fidelity with a significantly accelerated training process.

papers.title: Fatigue Life Prediction of Laser Shock Peened LPBF Steel Considering Surface Defects and Residual Stress Relaxation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Laser shock peening (LSP) is an advanced surface strengthening technique that improves the fatigue resistance of laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) metallic components by introducing compressive residual stress and modifying surface microstructure. However, accurate fatigue life prediction remains challenging due to the influence of defects and residual stress relaxation. In this study, a fatigue life prediction model is developed by considering residual stress evolution and defect‐induced stress concentration. The model integrates residual stress prediction derived from LSP parameters with an analytical formulation based on local stress–strain theory to describe stress redistribution. Defect‐induced stress concentration is incorporated and characterized by surface valley depth and curvature. The results indicate that although higher LSP energy increases local stress concentration due to sharper surface valleys, the enhanced and more stable compressive residual stress dominates fatigue performance. The model provides a predictive tool for fatigue design and LSP strengthening strategies of additive manufacturing components.

papers.title: Koopman operator-augmented physics-informed neural network with SEI kinetics for stable and explainable SOH estimation in battery packs
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of State of Health (SOH) is pivotal for battery management, yet existing data-driven methods often lack physical interpretability and struggle with generalization under complex operating conditions. To bridge the gap between data-driven flexibility and electrochemical mechanism consistency, this paper proposes a Koopman Operator-Augmented Physics-Informed Neural Network (Koopman-PINN) tailored for battery pack SOH estimation. Unlike traditional black-box models, the proposed method embeds the nonlinear SOH degradation into a high-dimensional Koopman observation space where it evolves linearly. Crucially, the Solid Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) growth kinetics and boundedness conditions are embedded as physical loss terms. A spectral domain constraint is further imposed on the Koopman operator matrix, which forces all eigenvalues inside the unit circle (|λi| < 1) and constrains their phase angles to guarantee the physical consistency and long-term stability of the degradation trajectory. Furthermore, the SEI degradation rate coefficient α is treated as an independent trainable parameter, enabling the end-to-end learning of physical parameters. Validated on extensive battery pack datasets under quasi-constant temperature (804 cycles) and variable temperature (667 cycles) conditions, the Koopman-PINN reduces the MAE by 46.0% and RMSE by 48.9% compared to standard PINNs in quasi-constant temperature. Under variable temperature conditions, Koopman-PINN reduces MAE by 30.0% and RMSE by 29.6% compared to the traditional PINN. Notably, the learned activation energy (≈30 kJ/mol) aligns well with the physical laws of SEI growth, and the spectral analysis reveals distinct dynamical modes governing the degradation process, providing a novel interpretable perspective on battery aging mechanisms.

However, SLM-fabricated components, especially those containing locally complex surface regions, often suffer from burrs, balling, microcracks, and tensile residual stress (TRS). These issues are difficult to eliminate by conventional machining or heat treatment (HT) alone. Consequently, such defects degrade fatigue performance and restrict the practical engineering application of SLM-fabricated components. This study proposed a novel direct surface post-processing method utilizing microscale laser shock peening without coating (μLSPwC) for locally complex surface regions of SLM-fabricated components. The process was designed to combine laser-induced local micro-melting for surface defect mitigation with shock-induced plastic deformation for near-surface strengthening. SLM-fabricated 17-4PH (AISI 630, UNS S17400) stainless steel, TC4 (Ti-6Al-4V) titanium alloy, and GH4169 (Inconel 718, UNS N07718) nickel-based superalloy were treated to assess the impact of μLSPwC on surface morphology, roughness, residual stress, microhardness, and rotating bending fatigue life. The surface roughness of all three materials dropped more than 20% after treatment. Furthermore, μLSPwC introduced compressive residual stress (CRS) layers and hardened layers exceeding 300 μm. The rotating bending fatigue life was improved by more than 20 times, and in some cases by over two orders of magnitude, at the selected stress levels. Therefore, μLSPwC is a promising post-processing technique for locally complex surface regions on SLM-fabricated components, particularly in situations where hot isostatic pressing, HT, or conventional surface machining is impractical or ineffective.

papers.title: Designing High-Entropy Alloys: From Physical Metallurgy to Machine Learning Enabled Discovery
papers.abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are characterized by having more than one principal element, in contrast to a traditional alloy with only one base element; this provides a much wider composition space compared to traditional alloys; hence, HEAs have been the most studied metal alloys in the last couple of decades. This review links the fundamentals of these materials to the data-driven methods now used to design them. The first part of this review describes the fundamentals of these materials, including the thermodynamic and kinetic basis of these materials and an entropy-based classification. The subsequent parts of this review describe the synthesis routes of these materials via liquid-state, solid-state, gas-state, and other processing routes. The choice of processing route can have a significant impact on the resulting material, including the phase(s) formed, the chemical homogeneity, and contamination of the material. We have systematically reviewed the mechanical, corrosion, thermal, electrical, and soft magnetic properties of these HEAs. In the final section, we discuss how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) can be used to solve the problem of combinatorial explosion of the design space of HEAs: supervised classifiers for phase prediction, regression and ensemble models for hardness, strength, and elastic moduli, active learning and Bayesian optimization for closed-loop discovery, high-throughput screening with CALPHAD, and machine-learned interatomic potentials. We conclude with continuing constraints such as lack of data, noisy labels, and poor encoding of process history, and areas of development including transfer learning, generative design, and self-driving laboratories.

papers.title: On the scaling-up of 3D-printed metallic POCS structured catalysts membrane reactors
papers.abstract: This work reports the first experimental demonstration of a scaled-up multi-membrane reactor for ammonia synthesis, integrating four tubular carbon molecular sieve membranes (CMSMs) with two 3D-printed metallic Periodic Open Cellular Structure (POCS) supports of Gyroid and Body-Centred Cubic (BCC) geometry, manufactured in Inconel 625 by Laser Powder Bed Fusion and washcoated with a Ru-based catalyst via a scaled-up dip-spin coating procedure. The coating protocol transferred to both topologies at the larger scale without modification, with optical microscopy confirming uniform, crack-free coverage.. Novolac-based CMSM carbonized at 550 °C were characterised by organic elemental analysis, XPS, and Raman spectroscopy, confirming a defect-rich, turbostratic sp 2 carbon matrix with microporous architecture. Baseline testing in the conventional reactor over 350–450 °C and 20–40 bar(g) demonstrated that Gyroid and BCC configurations deliver virtually identical catalytic performance, reflecting the dominance of reaction kinetics and thermodynamics over geometry-dependent transport resistances. Upon membrane integration, this geometry-independence was preserved, and the membrane consistently enhanced NH 3 production rates across all operating conditions. Beyond-equilibrium operation, with H 2 conversion and NH 3 yield reproducibly exceeding thermodynamic limits, was achieved exclusively at low wight hourly space velocity (WHSV) and a sweep ratio (SW) of 4: H 2 conversion surpassed equilibrium by 30% at 400 °C and 110% at 450 °C, with NH 3 yield gains of 65% and 170% over the conventional reactor. Scaling from one to four membranes yielded a membrane-area-normalised productivity improvement of up to 424% at 350 °C and 40 bar(g), providing a strong foundation for continued scale-up of membrane reactors for ammonia synthesis.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for renewable‑dominated energy systems: A scoping review
papers.abstract: The growing global demand for clean, reliable and low‑carbon electricity is driving a rapid transformation towards renewable‑dominated energy systems. This scoping review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the renewable energy value chain, with a focus on solar, wind, hydropower and hydrogen, as well as energy storage and smart grids. Following the PRISMA‑ScR framework, we systematically searched Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect and Web of Science for peer‑reviewed studies published over the last 15 years that apply machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning or other AI techniques to energy generation, forecasting, grid operation, storage management and decarbonisation strategies. The included literature shows that AI models consistently outperform classical baselines for renewable power forecasting, hybrid renewable energy system optimisation, and predictive maintenance of critical assets, often yielding substantial improvements in accuracy, efficiency and operational flexibility. At the same time, deployment at scale is constrained by data quality and availability, computational cost, model interpretability, cybersecurity concerns and gaps in regulatory and market design. Emerging work on explainable AI and physics‑informed learning offers promising avenues to increase transparency, robustness and trust in high‑stakes energy applications. Drawing together results across technologies and tasks, the review identifies priority directions for future research, including interoperable data infrastructures, scalable and energy‑efficient AI architectures, integrated uncertainty quantification and explainability, and socio‑technical studies on governance and energy justice. These findings highlight AI’s potential to enable more intelligent, resilient and equitable renewable‑dominated energy systems, while underscoring the need for coordinated advances in technology, policy and practice.
